owned_child.routing: owned child(native-3) -> operator 192.168.100.170:44833 (own frame proxy) -> repair hub :18080

owner_reference.note: owned child Agent uses the exact repair Agent binary; the process owner is the harness on native-3

duplicate.scenario: a real Desired State change (script v1 -> v2) whose real-time CHANGE_NOTIFICATION frame was delivered TWICE by the harness proxy

out_of_order.scenario: two seams on the owned child link: (a) a stale CHANGE_NOTIFICATION replayed after a newer change, (b) a genuinely deferred (older) CHANGE_NOTIFICATION released only after the newer one had already been delivered

prune.scenario: an owned script+task were really deleted on the Hub; the connected Agent must prune them through the normal sync (tombstones)

seam.how: the owned child Agent was stopped and its OWN local store revision was set first to the smallest positive value (1) and then to 0, then restarted, so the Agent really asked the Hub with a maximally stale `since`; the global changelog_window setting and the global revision sequence were never written

boundary_proof.reason_not_reachable: the repair Hub global revision (2652) is far below changelog_window (5000), so no Agent-side `since` value can satisfy current - since > window while since > 0; writing the global changelog_window setting and mass-advancing the global revision are both excluded by the batch constraints

idempotency.note: settle window after every seam: duplicate / deferred / replayed notifications, a real deletion prune and two maximally-stale recoveries must not create duplicate objects or duplicate Executions
